verdictStatement: The single envelope6 delta at /allOf/19/then is a correct, minimal and strictly additive expression of the owned D9 interrupted class for an invocation interrupted before any committed Run. The gap RP-OBL-C01 is real, not assumed. The acceptance is conditional and is not a promotion. Parent envelope5 is still an unaccepted report04 candidate. Owner prose at workflows-and-surfaces.md:1340-1341 still requires nonempty errors and must be amended with the selection (F1). A committed-Run erasure cannot be detected at shape level and needs a named host admission join (F2). Whether the claimed Run-bearing carrier covers after-commit interruption on query-class commands is unverified (F3).

common:3 DomainDetailCode has 315 codes and none names interruption, cancellation or a signal. 314 of them are shape-admitted beside an interrupted termination, so the only v5 route is an unrelated detail, which is the invention the owner forbids ('DomainDetailCode is explanatory detail beside an existing code, never a termination code', workflows-and-surfaces.md:1367).
The UNKNOWN_OPTION form with an 'interrupted' diagnostic is shape-admitted in both majors but misstates class, code and exit, so it is not a lawful substitute.

kind=run requires run and kind=doctor requires DoctorResult (both command-specific). kind=query and kind=mutation require their records. kind=meta forces success/0. A fabricated run envelope before a Plan/Run exists is forbidden (workflows-and-surfaces.md:1344).

kind=invocation requires a full invocation:3 record (workflow, mode, orderedSteps). No pinned owner text binds it as the aggregate output of arbitrary commands. It is not treated as a lawful substitute, but that is owner reading, not a schema proof (see O2).

ownerLawAssessment.d9: Follows. workflows-and-surfaces.md:1355-1364 pairs interrupted with 130 and requires signal, with runId only when a Run was committed. The new form fixes class=interrupted, a D9Signal, exit 130 and no runId. The top-level StepTermination still applies as well.
ownerLawAssessment.cancellation: Follows. workflows-and-surfaces.md:224-228: before-settle gives interrupted 130 and names an earlier committed Run; after-settle is not reclassified. The schema cannot observe phase. The new form is lawful only for before-settle with no committed Run, and the contract assigns that selection to the host.
ownerLawAssessment.aggregateShape: Consistent with the report04 aggregate law {interrupted, signal, runId of last committed analysis}. With no committed analysis this is exactly {class, signal}, so closing executionId, authority, coverageId and domainDetail is correct for the aggregate. This narrowing applies only to the new alternative.
ownerLawAssessment.ledger: Unaffected. invocation:3 stepResults and Cancellation are separate records, and the envelope form does not erase step outcomes.
ownerLawAssessment.noNewVocabulary: Confirmed. No new code, detail, kind, identity, class or signal. The only schema-level vocabulary change is major 6.

highlights: All 3 signals are admitted in v6 and refused in v5. The form with all optional correlation fields (clientCorrelationId at 128 chars, projectId, projectRoot) is admitted in v6 and refused in v5.

Refused in both majors: null for errors, clientCorrelationId, projectId, requestId, termination, exitCode, kind and signal; clientCorrelationId empty or 129 chars; errors {}; termination as array; unknown top-level key; kind absent.

Refused on the new form: termination extras runId, executionId, authority, coverageId, domainDetail, errorCode, phase; exits 0, 2 and 4; success/operational-failed/policy-failed/indeterminate classes at exit 130; errors=[] under every other kind; hybrids between UNKNOWN_OPTION and interruption.
The old UNKNOWN_OPTION form is admitted in both majors. Its mutants (no or empty diagnostics, exit 4, another code, added signal, added run) are refused in both.
Byte level: a duplicate 'errors' key and exit 130.0 are refused by canonical.parse (AdmissionError).
The report04 interrupted kind=run golden (runId retained) is admitted in both majors. Adding errors=[] is refused. kind=failure keeping runId is refused, even with every payload stripped.
Superset over 46 values (43 metadata fixtures, base, UNKNOWN_OPTION, golden): no value admitted in v5 is refused in v6. The only v6-only value is the new form.
probes.evidenceQualityNote: Several root 'new-form-no-*' probes (run {}, meta {}, query {}, availability {}) use placeholder payloads that fail their own schemas, so they do not show the new `not` clause is load-bearing. The reviewer repeated them with owner-valid payloads: availability, findings, query and diagnostics are load-bearing in the `not` clause; run, advisoryReport, querySurface, queryRecord and meta are also refused by pre-existing allOf entries (defence in depth). retentionDisclosure, agentHints, mutation, doctor and invocation were not tested with owner-valid payloads. mutation, doctor and invocation are independently refused because their kinds require them and errors=[] forces kind=failure.

findings.blocking: blocks selection, not this conditional acceptance
findings.title: Durable owner prose still says kind=failure requires nonempty errors
findings.detail: workflows-and-surfaces.md:1340-1341 (pinned) says 'A kind=failure envelope requires a nonempty errors array of DomainDetail'. The pinned owner text also does not state the pre-existing metadata4 UNKNOWN_OPTION empty-errors exception. envelope6 widens that exception further. contract.md says no architecture owner file changes, and successor.json integrationDuties list report, CLI, inventory, registry and host rebinds but no owner-prose amendment. With the schema selected and the prose unchanged, the two owners would disagree.
findings.required: Before selection, add a duty to amend workflows-and-surfaces §8 (and its metadata successor text, if that is where the UNKNOWN_OPTION exception lives). The amendment names both empty-errors forms, the before-settle/no-committed-Run condition, and the ban on dummy Runs and invented details.

findings.title: A shape schema cannot detect a committed Run erased through the new form
findings.detail: The report04 interrupted kind=run golden, rewritten as kind=failure/errors=[] with run, runId and payloads removed, is admitted by v6. That is expected, because the schema cannot see the ledger. Preservation after commit therefore depends entirely on host admission joining the envelope termination to invocation:3 (cancellation.phase=before-settle, no committed analysis Run). report04 names J-LEDGER-AGGREGATE only for report-bearing documents. A plain json/agent/human envelope has no carried ledger.
findings.required: Name an envelope host-admission join (for example extend J-ENV-TERMINATION-RUN) that refuses the new form when the invocation ledger records a committed Run or a phase other than before-settle, and add refusal goldens for it.

findings.blocking: no (outside the stated scope, but the contract makes the claim)
findings.title: The Run-bearing interruption carrier is shown only for kind=run commands
findings.detail: contract.md says a previously committed Run 'follows the existing Run-bearing interruption carrier'. The evidence is the fit kind=run golden. Query-class commands that commit an analysis Run and then run a query step (report04 bases candidates-run, inspect-run, review-brief-run) have no demonstrated carrier for a before-settle interruption during the query step. kind=query requires a query record, kind=failure with runId still needs an unrelated detail, and the new form correctly forbids runId. RP-OBL-C01 as recorded in report04 is scoped to 'no committed Run', so this is not a defect of the delta. It is an unverified generalisation in the contract text.
findings.required: Either show that those commands lawfully emit kind=run carrying the committed AnalysisResult on interruption, or record a separate owner obligation. Do not widen the new form to runId.

findings.title: Root probe evidence for the payload `not` clause is weaker than it reads
findings.detail: See probes.evidenceQualityNote. The clause is correct. The root's placeholder-payload probes would pass even if most `not` members were deleted.
findings.required: When rebasing, use owner-valid payloads (for example from the report04 goldens) for each forbidden member, or record which members are redundant with existing allOf entries.

findings.title: Provenance standing must stay explicit
findings.detail: successor.json and the manifest correctly mark the proposal as unreviewed and unselected, conditional on the unaccepted report04 envelope5. inputs/envelope5.json is pinned to m1-report-projection-subject-04/owner, which is a candidate path, not a product owner path. This review does not change that standing. If report04 changes envelope5, this delta and its restoration check must be redone against the new parent bytes.
findings.required: Keep 'conditional on unaccepted envelope5' in any downstream record, and rebind parent sha256 on any report04 revision.

observations.text: projectRoot (a UserInputPath) is permitted on the new form as correlation. That matches the existing failure forms; path-disclosure policy is unchanged by this delta.

Exit/class pairing across envelope5 is host-checked ('the checker refuses any other pairing'). The new form pins 130 in schema, which is stricter than the rest of the envelope and harmless.
